lede: Regulatory reporting automation and data quality practices help reporting, controls, compliance, and data quality professionals make reporting checks more traceable. The course covers data profiling, quality checks, automated validation and reconciliation workflows, and lineage documentation. Participants practice creating scorecards, cleansing rules, control matrices, and dashboards to monitor exceptions and support remediation.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who already support reporting, controls, or data quality work and need a more structured approach to automation and governance. Regulatory Reporting Analysts who validate and submit recurring reports. Finance Control Specialists who reconcile source data and reporting outputs. Data Quality Analysts who track defects and remediation patterns. Compliance Managers who oversee reporting governance and escalation. Reporting Team Leads who coordinate approvals and submission calendars. Regulatory Operations Specialists who manage control evidence and exceptions. MIS Reporting Analysts who prepare management and regulatory data packs. Internal Control Analysts who test reporting checks and sign-offs. Data Governance Analysts who document lineage and ownership. Finance Transformation Specialists who automate reporting workflows.
modules: Data Quality Assessment with Great Expectations
prerequisites: You need a laptop, spreadsheet proficiency, and working familiarity with reporting extracts, reconciliations, and approval workflows. Prior exposure to control testing, data governance, or regulatory reporting is helpful, and no programming background is required.
